la:adj:intimus.html:
intĭmus, a, um,
adj. sup. [in-ter; cf. interior], inmost, innermost, most secret, most profound, most intimate (class.).
Lit.: traxit ex intimo ventre suspirium,from the deepest part,: in eo sacrario intimo,: in urbis intimam partem venisse,, § 96: abdidit se in intimam Macedoniam,: Tartara,: praecordia,: pectus,.—
Trop.
Adj.
Profound, inward, deepest, inmost: ex intima philosophia,: consilia,: cogitationes,: sermo,i. e. soliloquy,: animus,: artificium,: ars,: amicitia,: familiaritas,.—
Of persons, intimate, near: ex meis intimis familiaribus,: intimi ipsius amici,; ; : inter intimos amicos habere,: scis quam intimum habeam te,; . — With dat.: me fuisse huic fateor intimum,: Catilinae,: Clodio,.— With apud: facere se intimum apud aliquem,. —
Subst.: intĭmus, i, m., a most intimate friend: unus ex meis familiarissimis atque intimis,; cf. 3, 1, 3; ; : ex intimis regis,: intimi amicorum Vitellii, —
intĭma, ōrum, n., the inmost parts: finium,: scalpuntur intima versu,.— Sing. (rare): se in intimum conicere,.— Adv.: intĭmē, in the inmost part, inwardly, internally; most intimately, most cordially, most strongly (class. only in the trop. signif.).
Lit.: uri intime,; .—
Trop.: utebatur intime Q. Hortensio,was on terms of close intimacy with,: intime commendari,.

la:verb:intimo.gloss: to tell, relate, narrate, recount, describe, intimate
senses: to tell, relate, narrate, recount, describe, intimate
la:verb:intimo.html:
intĭmo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
intimus
,
toput or bring into (post-class.).
Lit.: partem gurgiti,: Nilus mari intimatur,flows into,; : argentum tabulis,.—
Transf.
To drive or press into: imaginem aliquam inbibere et sibi intimare,; . —
To announce, publish, make known, intimate: nuntius intimatur,; : vitam litteris, Treb. Gall. 16: notoriā tuā intimāsti, Claudium graviter irasci, Gall. ap. Treb. : cunctis pistoribus intimari oportet, quod si quis, etc., Cod. 14, 3, 1: longitudines syllabarum,; .
